newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight dips to 6.10/20 pct from 8.3.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight dips to 6.10/20 pct from 8.3.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell to 6.10/20 percent against 8.3 on Tuesday as liquidity returned to the system, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said foreign and large local banks were suddenly flush with funds, which pulled down the overnight rate after wild fluctuations between six and eight percent.
Many dealers with small banks said they were not sure where the liquidity came from.
"It has to be either overseas funds or some Bank Negara maturities of funds directly raised from select banks," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said the overnight rate opened at eight percent, dipped to around seven percent, recovered to 7.8 and then to 6.10.
Bank Negara regularly intervenes in the domestic market to control liquidity or set interest rates. It sometimes approaches select banks directly to raise deposits.
"No funds were expected. We expected overnight to remain firm today and ease tomorrow when some funds come in from overseas," said a dealer with another local bank.
He said the central bank was said to have sold dollars against ringgit on Tuesday. It takes two days for a spot foreign exchange transaction to be completed.
Earlier, short-term rates rose sharply despite adequate liquidity as the flush banks focused on long-term lending.
Dealers said one-week money was up at 7.45/50 percent against 6.90/7.00, two-week was at 7.45/50 against 7.00/10 and one-month at 7.25/30 against 7.20/22.
However, medium and long-term rates were nearly steady at the previous levels. Three-month money at 7.25/30 percent and six-month at 7.30/35 were both unchanged.
"Foreign and some big banks are lending longer-term because they view interest rates will be stable around this level," said a dealer with a local bank.
He said the market was short on funds up to one-month money though overall liquidity was adequate.
